==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|ꝓfit||abbreviation|obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*dʰeh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|profit}}, from {{der|en|fro|profit}} (Modern {{cog|fr|profit}}), from {{der|en|la|prōfectus||advance, progress, growth, increase, profit}}, from {{m|la|proficiō||to go forward, advance, make progress, be profitable or useful}}. {{doublet|en|profect}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|prŏfʹit|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɒfɪt/}}
* {{enPR|prŏʹfit|a=GA,Atlantic Canada}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɑfɪt/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-profit.ogg|a=California}}
* {{enPR|prŏfʹit|a=CA,Boston,Maine}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɒfɪt/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɔfɪt/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɒfət/|[ˈpɹɔ̟fət]|a=NZ}}
* {{homophones|en|prophet}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒfɪt|s=2}}
* {{hyphenation|en|prof|it}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|accounting|economics}} Total [[income]] or [[cash flow]] minus [[expenditure]]s, i.e., the [[money]] or other [[benefit]] a non-governmental organization or individual receives in exchange for products and services sold at an advertised price.
#* '''1750 Oct. 2''', {{w|Samuel Johnson}}, ''{{w|The Rambler}}'':
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1935|author=w:Smedley Butler|title=w:War Is a Racket|pages=1 & 7
|passage=War is a racket. It always has been. It is possibly the oldest, easily the most [[profitable]], surely the most vicious. It is the only one international in scope. It is the only one in which the '''profits''' are reckoned in [[dollar]]s and the losses in lives... Of course, it isn't put that crudely in war time. It is dressed into speeches about patriotism, love of country, and "we must all [[put one's shoulder to the wheel|put our shoulders to the wheel]]," but the '''profits''' jump and leap and skyrocket—and are safely pocketed.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=68| magazine=w:The Economist| titleurl=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time|title=T time| passage=The ability to shift '''profits''' to low-tax countries by locating intellectual property in them, which is then licensed to related businesses in high-tax countries, is often assumed to be the preserve of high-tech companies. […] current tax rules make it easy for all sorts of firms to generate […] “stateless income”: '''profit''' subject to tax in a jurisdiction that is neither the location of the factors of production that generate the income nor where the parent firm is domiciled.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027215946/https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2013/06/22/t-time}}
# {{lb|en|dated|literary}} Benefit, positive result obtained.
#: {{ux|en|Reading such an enlightening book on the subject was of much '''profit''' to his studies.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|1 Corinthians|vii|35|text=This I speak for your own '''profit'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|IV|ii|passage=if you dare do yourself a '''profit''' and a right}}
# {{senseid|en|interest in land}} {{lb|en|property law}} {{ellipsis of|en|profit à prendre}}.

====Usage notes====
* Regarding the income sense, when the difference is negative, the term ''[[loss]]'' is preferred. But ''negative profit'' does appear in [[microeconomics]].
* Profit by a government agency is called a [[surplus]].

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|gain}}

====Antonyms====
* {{l|en|loss}}
